# 35_commit_files.sh - Commit and push only the given files

<!-- BEGIN pipeline-callers: generated by tools/automation_doc_links.py, do not edit by hand -->
:::{attention} Usually run by a Bitbucket pipeline
`35_commit_files.sh` is normally not run on its own. The Bitbucket pipelines listed below call it as one step of a longer job, after earlier steps have prepared its inputs and environment. Run it by hand mainly for debugging or local testing.

**Called from [bitbucket-pipelines.yml](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/replication-template/blob/master/bitbucket-pipelines.yml):**

## Description

Commits exactly the files named on the command line on top of the branch as it is on Bitbucket, and pushes. For steps that add their own files to a repository that others push to as well, such as [`p-pii-checker`](#pipeline-p-pii-checker).

The commit is built in a separate index, starting from the remote branch tip. Nothing else in the working tree goes into it, and the working tree is neither merged nor rebased, so other changes in the checkout (logs, file modes, the deposit) can neither block the push nor end up in the commit. If the push is rejected because someone pushed in the meantime, the commit is rebuilt on the new tip; up to five attempts, waiting 5, 10, ... seconds in between. If the files are already on the branch as they are, nothing is committed.

Compare [32_pull_push.sh](help-32_pull_push), which pulls the remote branch into the checkout and pushes everything committed there.

## Usage

```bash
./automations/35_commit_files.sh "Adding pii-checker results" \
    generated/pii_checker_results-nodetails.xlsx generated/pii_checker_summary.txt
```

### Environment Variables

- `jiraticket` - If set, the message is prefixed with `<ticket> #comment [skip ci]`; otherwise with `[skip ci]`.
- `BITBUCKET_BRANCH` - Branch to push to (default: the current branch).
